## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 11, also known as the *Garupāvuraṇa-sikkhāpada*, is a monastic training rule from the Vinaya Piṭaka governing the conduct of Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunī*s) [SuttaCentral]. The rule addresses the requisition or exchange of an excessively expensive, heavy outer cloak or robe (*garupāvuraṇa*), prescribing that a nun who asks for such a garment must forfeit it and confess the infraction [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying commentary is available by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule possesses extensive parallels across diverse early Buddhist vinaya lineages [SuttaCentral]. Curated parallels listed by SuttaCentral include the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra counterparts, Sanskrit Lokottaravāda Vinaya (san-lo-bi-vb-np19), Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya texts (xct-mu-bi-vb-np32 and xct-mu-bi-pm-np32), as well as Chinese translations belonging to the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Mahāsāṅghika traditions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of this text with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records widespread formulaic reuse, most noticeably with its adjacent companion rule on light cloaks, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 12 (§1.1–2.3.11 ↔ §1.1–2.2.11 with 0.94 similarity), alongside other Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules in both the Bhikkhunī and Bhikkhu Vibhaṅgas (e.g., Bi-Vb Np10, Bi-Vb Np5, and Bu-Vb Np6) and the Bhesajjakkhandhaka of the Khandhakas [DharmaNexus].
